question: What is the primary setting for the delivery of home health care services?
explanation: Home health care specifically brings professional nursing and health services directly to individuals living in their private residences. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: How does home health care primarily impact crowded tertiary health facilities?

options.A: It helps alleviate hospital congestion by managing stable patients outside wards
options.B: It increases the average length of stay for acute inpatients
options.C: It completely replaces the need for emergency surgical departments
options.D: It forces hospitals to close outpatient clinics permanently

explanation: By shifting stable care needs out of the facility, home health care frees up beds and resources in congested hospitals. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which advantage is directly associated with avoiding long-term hospital stays through home care?

options.B: Immediate access to emergency surgical theatres
options.C: Elimination of all out-of-pocket medication costs
options.D: Guaranteed elimination of chronic disease symptoms

explanation: Staying outside hospital walls protects patients from acquiring secondary infections common in institutional environments. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: Why does home care generally enhance the psychological well-being of elderly patients?

options.A: it prevents them from ever experiencing physical pain
options.B: It keeps them within a familiar environment close to personal belongings
options.C: It guarantees that family members will perform all clinical procedures
options.D: It completely removes the need for any future medical appointments

explanation: Familiar surroundings reduce confusion and emotional stress, promoting a positive mental outlook during recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is a primary economic advantage of home health care over traditional hospital admission?

options.A: Removal of all indirect transportation expenses
options.B: Permanent exemption from purchasing prescribed medications
options.C: Elimination of high institutional bed and overhead charges
options.D: Free provision of all medical equipment by the government

explanation: Patients do not incur daily facility accommodation fees when receiving care inside their own homes. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: Which factor frequently creates an unexpected financial burden for families managing home care in developing regions?

options.A: Procuring auxiliary equipment like backup power generators and special beds
options.B: Covering mandatory malpractice insurance for visiting nurses
options.C: Paying mandatory hourly taxes directly to local nursing councils
options.D: Renting specialized hospital wings for weekend monitoring

explanation: In areas with infrastructure challenges, families often shoulder the cost of purchasing supportive equipment to make home care viable. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is a major clinical limitation of managing patients at home?

options.A: Inability of nurses to administer any oral medications
options.B: Mandatory requirement for daily physician visits
options.C: Absence of immediate multidisciplinary emergency resuscitation teams
options.D: Strict prohibition against family members entering the room

explanation: Homes do not possess the rapid response teams and immediate emergency equipment found in hospital setups. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recognized disadvantage or limitation of home health care?

options.A: Limited availability of complex diagnostic laboratory equipment on-site
options.B: Potential delays during emergency transfers caused by poor transit infrastructure
options.C: Risk of caregiver burnout from continuous physical and emotional demands
options.D: Guaranteed 24-hour access to advanced surgical theaters in the bedroom

explanation: Advanced surgical facilities are exclusive to hospitals and are never available within a standard home care setting. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which environmental hazard is a community health nurse most likely to encounter during a home visit?

options.A: Unrestrained pets and structural safety hazards

explanation: Private residences lack the standardized safety infrastructure and controlled environments of institutional hospitals. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why must community nurses practice specific safety protocols during home visits?

options.A: Patients are legally permitted to detain medical staff overnight
options.B: Hospital management strictly forbids them from leaving the vehicle
options.C: They are legally required to carry firearms for personal protection
options.D: They operate in uncontrolled environments without immediate backup security

explanation: Lone workers in community health face unpredictable home settings and must proactively manage their personal safety. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is accurate documentation especially critical in home health nursing?

options.A: It is used exclusively by insurance companies to deny patient claims
options.B: It protects the nurse against legal liability and tracks continuous care
options.C: It replaces the need for verbal handovers between shift teams
options.D: It is legally required to be published in public health journals

explanation: Because home care is decentralized, clear documentation provides a legal record of care delivered and patient status. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: A home care nurse frequently faces ethical tension when a competent patient refuses a recommended treatment plan. What principle must the nurse primarily navigate?

options.A: Immediate abandonment of the case without informing the agency
options.B: Transferring financial ownership of the home to the hospital
options.C: Forcibly administering the treatment to avoid legal prosecution
options.D: Balancing patient autonomy against the professional duty of care

explanation: Competent patients have the right to refuse care, requiring nurses to respect autonomy while providing safety education. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting an initial environmental assessment before starting home care?

options.A: To identify and mitigate potential safety risks in the home
options.B: To determine how many television sets the family owns
options.C: To calculate the exact market value of the patient's property
options.D: To redecorate the living room to match hospital standards

explanation: Initial assessments help spot hazards like poor lighting, stairs, or pets so they can be addressed before nursing care begins. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h7)

question: How can nursing teams best address the common problem of family caregiver exhaustion?

options.A: Integrating structured respite care and educational support into the plan
options.B: Instructing family members to stop visiting the patient entirely
options.C: Transferring all care responsibilities to untrained neighbors
options.D: Increasing the frequency of daily nursing visits to twelve hours

explanation: Respite care gives exhausted family members temporary relief, preventing burnout and sustaining long-term home care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h7)
